subject: Order Form indemnity sequencing — triage & litigation-fallthrough scenarios
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@brightport.com>

Cc: Aiden Cole <aiden.cole@brightport.com>, legal@brightport.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Redwood order form — indemnity sequencing proposal

Soojin —

Thanks again for walking through the draft yesterday. Attached is BrightPort's redline (BrightPort_redline_v2.pdf) focusing on the order-form indemnity language we discussed. High-level points we redlined:

- We propose splitting defense/control by claim type: (i) Customer data/PII claims --> BrightPort controls; (ii) Third-party IP infringement claims tied to model outputs --> shared-notice with defense-control presumptions that favor BrightPort for direct infringement but carve back for agent/derivative scenarios.
- Monetary cap language: BrightPort is comfortable with an order-form-specific cap tied to prior 12-month spend but wants the MSA to preserve broader indemnities for willful misconduct and IP allegations.
- Escrow/holdback trigger: proposed 30-day escrow on disputed indemnity amounts when litigation notice is provided.

Two asks from us: 1) can Redwood provide a practical evidence routing matrix we can include (who owns takedown, who will run privilege reviews), and 2) can you confirm whether Redwood's SOC2/audit logs will include per-request model version IDs and prompt metadata for the relevant retention window?

Attached: BrightPort_redline_v2.pdf; evidence-routing-matrix.xlsx (stub).

Happy to hop on a quick call if needed.

—Julia
Julia Park
Head of Legal Operations, BrightPort

Subject: Re: Redwood order form — indemnity sequencing proposal

Julia —

Thanks for the redline and the clear asks. We're reviewing with legal and infra; preliminary responses below and we'll attach a short exec summary to the redline.

- Defense/control split: we can accept a tiered approach that ties control to whether BrightPort is an alleged direct infringer (BrightPort customer activity) vs. model-generated third-party content. For the latter, Redwood will not concede blanket defense-control but can accept a rebuttable presumption where BrightPort gets first control for a limited category of claims.

- Cap: Redwood's standard is to tie order-form caps to committed monthly spend x 12 (with an absolute floor). We can do a narrower order-form carve if BrightPort accepts a mutual limitation for derivative-agent claims.

- Escrow: 30-day short-term hold is reasonable if we get clear escalation rules and a cap on aggregate escrow amounts per calendar year.

On evidence/observability: yes, SOC2 logs include model version IDs and request timestamps; prompt metadata retention is configurable per private deployment. We'll attach our audit-log sample and a short evidence-routing matrix.

Next steps: I'll pull Ben (sales) for commercial framing and loop Karthik/Kimberly for the working redline. If you can do a short version that enumerates the three claim buckets you care about (customer-owned code, customer-supplied data, model-output third-party IP) that will speed alignment.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of GTM Legal — Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood order form — indemnity sequencing proposal

Soojin / Julia / team —

Following internal review, here is a suggested compromise redline (attached as tracked comments in OrderForm_v1-3.docx):

1) Claim buckets (simple definitions):
   - Customer Data Claims: claims arising from BrightPort's customer data or code — BrightPort controls defense.
   - Model-Output Direct Infringement: where a third party asserts direct copyright/patent claim tied to a discrete model output attributable to BrightPort's prompts or dataset — presumptive shared-notice; BrightPort may request control where evidence shows direct correlation.
   - Model-Service Abuse / Derivative Claims: claims from aggregated model behavior or third-party training data — Redwood defends or reimburses per MSA with reimbursement cap.

2) Control mechanics: if BrightPort requests control for Model-Output Direct Infringement, Redwood reserves right to appoint counsel if: (a) BrightPort's proposed counsel has conflict or (b) Redwood reasonably believes a material defense strategy would be compromised. Redwood will not unreasonably withhold consent.

3) Escrow/holdback: 30-day temporary hold on disputed indemnity payments, release after (i) mutual covenant to litigate or (ii) settlement. Aggregate annual escrow exposure capped at 2x the last 12 months' net fees.

4) Evidence routing: Redwood will respond to formal takedown/evidence requests within 48 hours and provide model run-ids, prompt hashes, and model-version metadata where available; full prompt text requires a standard discovery request and appropriate confidentiality protections.

I kept the language deliberately modular so it can map to both Hosted and Private deployments. Attaching OrderForm_v1-3.docx and a short redline summary.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Julia Park <julia.park@brightport.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: aiden.cole@brightport.com, legal@brightport.com
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood order form — indemnity sequencing proposal

Karthik / Soojin —

Thanks — the structure helps. A few clarifying points before I take back to our exec legal:

- We need explicit timing on evidence delivery: BrightPort expects the model run-ids and metadata within 48 hours of a preserved notice; please confirm Redwood's SLA for partial/complete production.
- The escrow cap of 2x ARR is broadly acceptable in principle but our procurement team will ask for a smaller multiplier tied to committed monthly spend — would Redwood accept 1.5x committed annual spend instead?
- On counsel appointment: BrightPort needs language that gives it control if the claim relates solely to BrightPort customer content or configurations. The proposed carve for discovery-necessitated prompt text requiring formal discovery is acceptable.

If we can land these three items, I can escalate to our GC for sign-off and then route to procurement for an economical order-form price lock. Would Redwood be open to a single 30-minute call to finalize the numeric escrow multiplier and the SLA timing?

Attachments: redline-exec-summary.txt (stub).

—Julia
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Redwood order form — indemnity sequencing proposal

Julia —

Yes to the call. Ben will coordinate a 30-minute slot tomorrow; proposed attendees: Soojin, Karthik, Kimberly (legal), Ben (AM), Julia, Aiden (procurement).

Pre-answers:
- Evidence delivery SLA: Redwood confirms 48hrs for run-ids & metadata for preserved notices; partial productions will be flagged with scope notes. Full prompt text requires discovery/court order.
- Escrow multiplier: Redwood can agree to 1.5x committed annual spend as an alternative to the 2x aggregate cap, provided BrightPort accepts a reconciliation clause tied to annual spend revisions.
- Counsel control carve: acceptable where claim exclusively arises from BrightPort-supplied code/data; Redwood retains appointment rights where cross-party issues arise.

I'll attach the audit-log sample and the evidence-routing matrix in the meeting invite. Thanks — let's get this across the finish line.

Best,
Soojin
